name: Alibaba Group Holding Limited
monetization: Sells AI cloud (Qwen model family, GPU/inference services) through Alibaba Cloud, funded by e-commerce cash flows and a RMB 380B+ AI capex program.
description_md: Alibaba is China's largest cloud provider (Cloud Intelligence Group) and e-commerce platform, and the anchor of China's open-model ecosystem via its Qwen family — the most-adopted open-weight models domestically and a top global open-source line. It is also a strategic investor across China's AI labs (Moonshot, Zhipu, MiniMax, 01.AI) and designs in-house accelerators through T-Head. In February 2025 it announced a three-year RMB 380B (~$53B) AI/cloud capex program — the largest disclosed in China — which management said in May 2026 it will 'overshoot'.
ai_monetization_md: AI-related product revenue (model APIs, GPU/inference cloud, AI-enhanced products) has posted **triple-digit y/y growth for 11 consecutive quarters** through the March 2026 quarter. Cloud Intelligence Group revenue grew 38% y/y in the March quarter (external revenue +40%), with AI products at ~30% of external cloud revenue. Monetization runs through consumption-based cloud contracts rather than seat licenses — Qwen's open-weights strategy sacrifices license fees to drive cloud consumption and standards adoption. The cost side is heavy: FY2026 profit fell sharply on AI infrastructure investment and e-commerce subsidies.
ai_strategy_md: Full-stack sovereign-scale AI: own models (Qwen 3.x), own silicon (T-Head) plus domestic accelerators to hedge US export controls, massive capex (RMB 380B program, to be exceeded — CEO Eddie Wu frames AI as a once-in-a-generation platform shift with returns visible over 3–5 years), and equity stakes across China's frontier labs. Alibaba is positioning as the AWS-plus-OpenAI of the Chinese bloc as US chips exit the market.
risk_notes_md: **Export-control frame:** Nvidia's H20 was banned (Apr 2025), re-licensed (Jul 2025) with a 15%-of-China-revenue payment to the US government, then effectively re-blocked as Beijing discouraged purchases; the B30A/Blackwell class is blocked for China in 2026, and on Jun 1, 2026 US bans were extended to Chinese firms' overseas data centers — directly constraining Alibaba Cloud's international expansion and pushing it onto domestic silicon (Huawei Ascend, Cambricon, T-Head) with lower performance per unit. **Margin risk:** FY2026 showed the AI buildout consuming e-commerce profits (quarterly profit fell sharply on capex and subsidies). **Geopolitical/listing risk:** dual NYSE/HKEX listing exposure.
